title: spec/data: `Object.titleFormat` is typed `template` dialect (declared `{{var}}`), but the only implementation reads single-brace `{field}` — and 71 of 73 in-repo authors write single-brace
body:
Found by the `os-dev` seat during the #15035 / #15028 author census (branch `claude/issue-15035-cron-dialect-author-census`, tree `f1e91595f`, 2026-09-05). Filed as a sub-issue of #15035 because it is the `template` half of that union's declared-versus-enforced question, but it is a separate defect and a separate decision: the census edits nothing. Unassigned; `domain:*`, type and priority are triage's.

## What the spec declares

`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts:2083` types `ObjectSchemaBase.titleFormat` with `TemplateExpressionInputSchema`. The dialect table in `packages/spec/src/shared/expression.zod.ts:23` says the `template` dialect is:

> `{{var}}` interpolation at evaluate time (same variable scope as CEL)

and names `titleFormat` as one of its uses. The `tmpl` tagged-template helper in the same file writes the same promise into its docblock (`{{record.x}}`, `{{os.user.id}}`).

## What is implemented

Measured in the sibling repo at the pinned sha — `.objectui-sha` = `a472b07167a39e55491109e864bb5a54027dcfbd`, and the checkout's HEAD is that same sha, so this is the objectui the console ships from.

`packages/core/src/utils/record-title.ts` `formatTitleTemplate` is the one interpolator (reached from `plugin-detail/src/DetailView.tsx:93`, `components/src/renderers/layout/containers.tsx:1898`, and the kanban / calendar title resolvers). It:

1. accepts either a bare string or the envelope, reading `.source`;
2. rewrites double braces DOWN to single — `template.replace(/\{\{\s*([^{}]+?)\s*\}\}/g, '{$1}')`, with the comment "Authoring tools and some legacy resolvers emit `{{…}}`";
3. then interpolates single-brace `{field}` / `{a.b}` against the record.

So the canonical grammar on the wire is single-brace record-field paths, and `{{…}}` is tolerated by being downgraded — the exact inverse of what the spec declares. There is no `{{ path | formatter }}` support (no `TEMPLATE_FORMATTERS`), and the variable scope is the record, not the CEL scope.

## What authors actually write

Brace-aware sweep over `packages/**`, `examples/**`, `content/docs/**`, `skills/**`, `docs/**` (generated trees, `dist`, `node_modules` and CHANGELOGs excluded), `f1e91595f`:

- 75 `titleFormat` value positions, 73 of them string literals.
- **71 single-brace**, e.g. `sys-user.object.ts:71` `'{name}'`, `sys-automation-run.object.ts:61` `'{flow_name} · {node_id}'`, `sys-record-share.object.ts:43` `'{object_name}/{record_id} → {recipient_id} ({access_level})'`.
- **2 double-brace**, both inside one lint test (`packages/lint/src/validate-record-title.test.ts:39, :76`).
- By tree: 38 `platform-objects`, 18 `plugins`, 11 `services`, 3 `lint`, 1 each `spec` / `metadata-protocol` / `cli`, 2 `docs`.
- **Zero in `examples/**`** — proven by control: `nameField` IS authored there (`examples/app-todo/src/objects/task.object.ts:209`), so the sweep reaches that tree; the examples have already migrated per ADR-0079.
- objectui itself authors a third spelling in a fixture: `packages/types/src/__tests__/object-schema-metadata-spec-derivation.test.ts:83` writes `'${subject}'`, which no interpolator resolves.

The hand-written docs are split against themselves: `content/docs/data-modeling/objects.mdx:69` and `schema-design.mdx:58` both teach `'{{record.name}} - {{record.code}}'`, while `docs/notes/crm-development-standards.mdx:97` teaches `'{field1} - {field2}'`. `docs/audits/2026-06-handwritten-docs-accuracy-followups.md:184` already recorded the mismatch and called it "spec-level reconciliation, not a doc fix", which is this card.

## Why it matters

Two separate things:

1. **Declared is not enforced, and the declaration is the wrong one.** The parse accepts any string, so neither grammar is checked; the docblock and the generated reference page (`content/docs/references/data/object.mdx:165`) promise a syntax the implementation treats as legacy. An AI author reading the spec writes `{{record.name}}`, which works only because the renderer downgrades it — and reading `{{record.name}}` back out of a real object file is impossible, because 71 of 71 shipped ones use the other spelling.
2. **It settles a ledger cell that was deliberately left open.** `packages/qa/dogfood/test/expression-conformance.ledger.ts` row `template-title-format` says the key's only interpolation site "is in the sibling repo objectui, which is not in this checkout: NOT measured here", and invites `enforced` once someone measures it. It is measured above: the site exists and is reached, so the row's `state` can move off `experimental` — but its `dialect` cell then becomes the lie, because what runs is not the `template` dialect.

## Not a decision — the shapes, for triage

- (a) Correct the declaration to what runs: give `titleFormat` its own single-brace record-path input schema (or keep `TemplateExpressionInputSchema` and fix the dialect table's `template` row to say the grammar is per-consumer). Cheapest, and honest.
- (b) Enforce the declared `{{var}}` grammar at parse time and migrate 71 authors. This is a Clause-2 accept-set narrowing on a published key with a real, large migration.
- (c) Retire the key under ADR-0049 / ADR-0079 D3, which already deprecates it in favour of `nameField` — a maintainer ruling, and the `spec-property-retirement` playbook's shape. Note the two `titleFormat` readers in objectui are ranked BELOW `nameField` in the same resolvers, so the retirement path is already half-built on the consumer side.

⛔ Do not read this card as proposing any of them; the spec lane holds the position on the whole dialect union (#15035 / #15028).

## Verified

- Dedup (2026-09-05, `search_issues`, semantic): zero results for the titleFormat grammar mismatch. Positive control in the same session returned #15035, #15028, #15027, #14825, #15527, #15430, #15811, #15867 — the whole expression family, closed cards included — so the zero is a reading, not a failure mode.
- The objectui reading is against the pinned sha, verified equal to that checkout's HEAD; it is not a second-hand claim.

Refs: #15035 · #15028 · #15027 · ADR-0079 · ADR-0049 · ADR-0058 D7.
